ai.literal: Having seen, heard, tasted, smelt, and touched, all five perceiving senses are present indeed within this bright-braceleted woman.
ai.translation: The pleasures of all five senses—sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch—are found together in this woman adorned with bright bracelets.
ai.modern: பார்த்தல், கேட்டல், உண்ணல், மோத்தல், தொடுதல் ஆகிய ஐந்து புலன்களாலும் அறியப்படும் இன்பங்கள் அனைத்தும் ஒளி பொருந்திய வளையல்களை அணிந்த இவளிடத்தே மட்டுமே உள்ளன.
ai.explanation: This couplet celebrates the ultimate sensory fulfillment found in the beloved. The poet lists the five modes of perception: seeing (kaṇṭu), hearing (kēṭṭu), tasting (uṇṭu), smelling (uyirttu), and touching (uṟṟu). While these five senses (aimpulanum) usually seek gratification from different sources, the lover experiences them all simultaneously in the presence of his beloved, referred to metonymically as the one wearing bright bracelets (oṇtoṭi). The sandhi of 'oḷ' (bright) and 'toṭi' (bracelet) naturally yields 'oṇtoṭi' through standard Tamil sound-merging rules.

ai.literal: For sickness, medicine is other things indeed; she who wears beautiful ornaments, for her own affliction, she herself is the medicine.
ai.translation: For ordinary diseases, the remedies lie in other external things; but for the affliction caused by this jewel-adorned maiden, she herself is the only cure.
ai.modern: நோய்க்கு மருந்துகள் வேறு பொருள்களாக இருக்கின்றன; ஆனால், ஆபரணங்களை அணிந்த இவள் தந்த நோய்க்கு இவளே மருந்தாக இருக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover contrasts physical illnesses with the sweet affliction of love. For any common physical sickness, the cure is found in external medicines like herbs. However, for the pain of longing caused by this beautifully adorned maiden, no external remedy works. She who created the affliction is herself the only medicine that can heal him through her presence and union.

ai.literal: Than sleeping on the soft shoulders of one's beloved, is it sweeter, the world of the lotus-eyed one?
ai.translation: Is the world of the lotus-eyed deity any sweeter than slumbering on the soft shoulders of one's beloved?
ai.modern: தாம் விரும்பும் காதலியின் மென்மையான தோள்களில் துயில்வதை விட, தாமரை போன்ற கண்களை உடைய இறைவனின் உலகம் இனிமையானதோ?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the speaker compares the ultimate spiritual or celestial bliss with the intimate joy of love. The phrase 'tām vīḻvār' refers to the beloved whom one desires, and 'meṉṟōḷ' describes her soft shoulders. By questioning whether the realm of the lotus-eyed deity is sweeter than sleeping in the embrace of the beloved, the poem exalts earthly love as a supreme experience that rivals or even surpasses divine realms.

ai.literal: If departing, it burns; when approaching, it feels cool; such a fire, where did she obtain, this woman?
ai.translation: Where did this woman obtain a fire that burns when one departs from it, but feels cool when one approaches?
ai.modern: விலகிச் சென்றால் சுடுகின்ற, நெருங்கி வந்தால் குளிர்ச்சி தருகின்ற நெருப்பை இவள் எங்கே பெற்றாள்?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the paradoxical nature of the beloved's touch. Ordinary fire burns when we get close to it and cools down when we move away. However, the lover notes that his partner's love acts in the exact opposite way: leaving her presence burns him with the pain of separation ('நீங்கின் தெறூஉம்'), while drawing near to her gives him a soothing, cool comfort ('குறுகுங்கால் தண்ணென்னும்'). He wonders in amazement where she could have acquired such a miraculous, unique fire ('தீ யாண்டுப் பெற்றாள் இவள்').

ai.literal: Like those very things at the moment they are desired, indeed resemble the shoulders of her who has flower-adorned hair.
ai.translation: The shoulders of my beloved, whose hair is adorned with flower petals, are like those objects of desire that yield fresh and exquisite pleasure every single time they are enjoyed.
ai.modern: பூவிதழ்கள் அணிந்த கூந்தலை உடையவளின் தோள்கள், நாம் விரும்பிய காலத்தில் அனுபவிக்கும் அந்தந்த இன்பப் பொருட்களைப் போல எப்போதும் புதிய இன்பத்தைத் தருகின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover expresses how the embrace of his beloved never grows old. He compares her shoulders to things that are intensely desired; just as those things bring fresh, unmatched joy every time they are experienced at the right moment, her shoulders offer a novel pleasure with every embrace. The phrase 'தோட்டார் கதுப்பினாள்' describes the beloved as one with flower-adorned hair, adding a sensory layer of fragrance and beauty to the imagery. The repetition of 'அவை அவை' (those very things) emphasizes the diverse and ever-renewing nature of these pleasures.

ai.literal: Whenever touching, for life to sprout, because of that touch, of the innocent girl, of nectar, are made, the shoulders.
ai.translation: Because her touch makes my life sprout with joy every time we meet, the shoulders of this innocent maiden must be made of nectar.
ai.modern: தொடும்போதெல்லாம் என் உயிர் தழைத்து எழும்புமாறு தீண்டுவதால், இந்தப் பேதையின் தோள்கள் அமிழ்தத்தினால் செய்யப்பட்டவை போலும்.
ai.explanation: The lover expresses the intense joy of physical union with his beloved. He says that whenever they touch, his life and spirit revive and flourish like a sprouting plant. Because her touch has this life-giving effect, he concludes that her shoulders must be fashioned out of 'amiḻtu' (the mythical nectar of immortality). The word 'pētai' here refers to his innocent, simple beloved, and 'uṟutōṟu' highlights that this rejuvenating effect happens every single time they embrace, never losing its freshness.

ai.literal: Staying in one's own home, sharing one's own food and eating, is like the embrace of this beautiful, golden-complexioned young woman.
ai.translation: The embrace of this beautiful, golden-complexioned young woman is like staying in one's own home and eating one's food after sharing it with others.
ai.modern: தன் சொந்த வீட்டில் இருந்து, தன் உணவைப் பிறருடன் பகிர்ந்து உண்பதைப் போன்றது, அழகிய மாமை நிறமுடைய இப்பெண்ணின் தழுவல்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the joy of the beloved's embrace to the ultimate domestic happiness. Living in one's own home and sharing one's food with others before eating represents the pinnacle of virtuous householder life. The poet suggests that the embrace of the beautiful, golden-complexioned young woman yields the same deep, wholesome, and guilt-free satisfaction. The word 'மா' refers to the beautiful mango-shoot-like golden complexion of the woman, which is highly praised in classical Tamil poetry.

ai.literal: To the two who love, sweet indeed is the embrace that does not allow the wind to pass in between.
ai.translation: Sweet indeed to two lovers is an embrace so close that even the wind cannot pass between them.
ai.modern: ஒருவரையொருவர் விரும்பும் இருவருக்கு, இடையில் காற்று கூடப் புக முடியாதபடி நெருக்கமாக இருக்கும் தழுவல் மிகவும் இனிமையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the physical and emotional closeness of lovers. The phrase 'வீழும் இருவர்' refers to two people who are deeply in love with each other. Their embrace ('முயக்கு') is described as being so tight and seamless that even the wind ('வளி') cannot find a gap to pass through ('போழப் படாஅ') or separate them. This vivid imagery emphasizes that true union leaves absolutely no room for distance or separation, making it the sweetest experience ('இனிதே') for the lovers.

ai.literal: Sulking, reconciling, and uniting—these are the fruit obtained by those who have united in love.
ai.translation: Feigned anger, reconciliation, and union—these are the rewards of love enjoyed by those who are united.
ai.modern: ஊடுதல், அதனை உணர்ந்து சமாதானம் அடைதல், பின்னர் கூடுதல் ஆகிய இவையே காதலில் இணைந்தவர்கள் பெறும் பயனாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the sweet cycle of intimacy that defines a loving relationship. The poet lists three key stages: 'ūṭal' (the feigned anger or sulking of lovers), 'uṇartal' (the realization and reconciliation that follows), and 'puṇartal' (their physical and emotional reunion). These three elements together constitute the ultimate fruit or benefit of love for those who are united. The verse highlights that the joy of love is not static, but is enriched by the playful tension of minor disagreements and the subsequent joy of making up.

ai.literal: Like seeing one's ignorance each time one learns, is love with the woman wearing beautiful jewels each time one unites closely.
ai.translation: Just as learning more and more only reveals one's previous ignorance, so does drawing closer to this beautifully jeweled woman only reveal new, deeper dimensions of love.
ai.modern: நூல்களைக் கற்கக் கற்க நம்முடைய அறியாமை விளங்குவது போல, சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த பெண்ணுடன் நெருங்கிப் பழகப் பழகக் காதல் இன்பம் மேலும் மேலும் புதியதாகத் தோன்றுகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the pursuit of knowledge with the experience of love. As a person learns more, they do not feel complete; instead, they realize how much they did not know before, exposing their own ignorance. Similarly, as the lover unites more closely with his beloved, he does not find satiation. Instead, each intimate union reveals new, previously unimagined depths of joy and desire, making him feel that his previous experience of love was incomplete.
